sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-Myc immunofluorescence without detergent permeabilisation confirmed extracellular display; no functional assay reported for this construct.
sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_shifted: insert_after_residue 74 -> 73 on human canonical Q96CP7 (paper numbering: ortholog:chicken, construct species: other:chicken). Paper (PMID 23673622): "a myc-tag was introduced after aminoacids 3, 42, 74, 107, 163, 201 and 252 of Calfacilitin". Audit note: Calfacilitin is chicken TLCD1 (UniProt F1NZP5, 252 aa; the paper's C-terminal tag 'after 252' fits chicken, not human 247 aa). Alignment: chick L74|S75 (LWQSPELL|SDIQ) = human L73|V74 (VWQTPDML|VEIE), offset -1, so human insert_after = 73 not 74. Deduced 6-TM N-out/C-out topology places loop 2 (tag 74) outside; the per-construct anti-myc result is only in Fig 3e (image), not text.] Residue 74 (V) falls in extracellular loop 1 (ECL1, landmarks 67–83), 8 residues from TM1 end (66) and 10 residues from TM2 start (84), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-clearance rule on both sides. The paper explicitly tested surface accessibility by anti-Myc staining without detergent in intact cells, directly validating this junction as extracellular. Python lookup confirms residue 74 = V and residue 75 = E in the canonical 247-aa sequence. PMC3674269 (Calfacilitin/TLCD1 topology study): Myc tag inserted after residue 74 of full-length Calfacilitin cloned into pcDNA3.1 and expressed in COS or HEK293T cells. Anti-Myc staining without detergent (extracellular-only condition) confirmed surface accessibility of this epitope.

sources.claim: A myc epitope was introduced into seven different locations between the predicted transmembrane domains, each construct introduced into either COS or HEK293T cells, which were then fixed and stained with anti-Myc either in the presence of detergent (to detect both intracellular and extracellular epitopes) or without detergent (for extracellular epitopes) ( Fig. 3 ).
sources.title: Calfacilitin is a calcium channel modulator essential for initiation of neural plate development
